pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks the seeded rows are all 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
src/index.js uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id. 'AC-2' covers both / and ?view=open with one item marked done.
'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'], which checks the filter, the id order and the ✓.
'AC-4' expects all three items in id order, with the done one marked and the others not.
'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for each of the three views and for /. The current view is a <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' sends Open, closed, an empty value and __proto__. Each answers 400 with no <li>. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
'AC-7' checks Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views once the table is empty. The code runs a COUNT only for an empty open or done view.
traffic/routes.json lists both views. 'AC-8' asserts they are present. The traffic worker passes ROUTES to a Request URL unchanged, so a query string works.

lenses.note: The spec has an owner go dated 2026-10-12. The change follows its decisions: open is the default view and the view is a query parameter.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and named by tests. All 6 state-table rows have a test under 'states'. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, so no later commit edits it.

I could not run `npm test` here because vitest is not installed. I read the tests instead. They assert rendered items, messages and status codes, and would fail against broken code. The traffic fake-app change is disclosed and does not weaken any assertion. tests/traffic-config.test.sh adds cases for a fragment, a space and a query string.
README describes the new views in the src/index.js line. Spec and README match the code.
The view is checked against an allowlist with Object.hasOwn. The SQL fragments come from constants. HTML output is escaped.
No injection path: the query parameter is only used as a key into a fixed map, and titles are escaped. No planted instructions found in the repository.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no stylesheet or client code. No UI design files are in the diff.
No browser flow is in the diff. The PR says no screenshots were taken.
The PR's claims match the diff: the 400 for other views, the empty-view messages, the routes check change, and the tests changed and added. The title is under 72 characters.
